C1.worst_defect: The hero says what it is and offers Live demo / Quick start, but nowhere on the home page does it say who builds or maintains VendurePOS (footer: only 'MIT licensed. Built with TallyUI. For Medusa, see MedusaPOS.'). It also never says who should not use it, such as a multi-store retailer that needs integrated card terminals or a cash drawer, so a buyer can't place it against Square or Shopify POS.
C1.where: home desktop 01-02 hero and footer; home.txt

C2.worst_defect: The home page sells an 'open-source till' that is 'MIT licensed', but building the till yourself 'needs your own RxDB Premium licence token in RXDB_PREMIUM' (a paid third-party licence). That is said only on Limitations and Connect a till, so in practice you depend on the hosted app.vendurepos.com, run by an unnamed operator whose analytics go to an unexplained ph.wcpos.com.
C2.where: home.desktop.02 footer vs limitations.desktop.01 bullet 3, connect-a-till.desktop.01 'The till's source is MIT-licensed...'

C3.worst_defect: The role the plugin's own 'New POS till key' button creates is missing ReadOrder on 0.3.0 ('On plugin 0.3.0 the role it creates (vendurepos-pos-till) has the step 4 permissions except ReadOrder, so add ReadOrder to that role yourself'). This is a known bug the docs work around in three places instead of a fixed release.
C3.where: quick-start.desktop.04 'Optional: a device key for each till'; connect-a-till.txt 'Give each cashier their own account' and 'Create and use a device key'

C4.worst_defect: At the till says 'A till key's role needs the TallyPosRefund permission, and the till role preset leaves it out'. But refunds at the till don't exist on any released plugin ('On plugin 0.3.0 an order shows no Refund items'), and the changelog never mentions TallyPosRefund, so the docs describe a permission no reader can find.
C4.where: at-the-till.txt 'Refund a sale' last paragraph vs changelog.desktop.01

C5.worst_defect: The 'What it does today' section is eight identical grey cards of the same weight. 'Keeps selling offline' and 'Every sale lands once', the two claims with proof links, look no different from 'Park a sale', so the differentiator doesn't stand out and the grid reads as a stock docs-template layout.

C6.worst_defect: Code blocks wrap rather than scroll on 390 px, so the generateMigration call breaks across five ragged lines ('generateMigration(config, { name: / 'AddVendurePos', outputDir: / './src/migrations' })'), which makes copy-reading hard. The quick start is a 10,000 px scroll with no collapse of the long troubleshooting text.

C7.worst_defect: Sitemap lastmod values are all build timestamps from the last day (e.g. home, at-the-till and limitations all 2026-11-18T07:49:49), so they say nothing about real content change. The 404 page logs a console 404 resource error and carries no JSON-LD (minor).

overall_worst.defect: 'MIT licensed' and 'open-source till' on the home page hide two facts a client would ask about first: the till can't be built without a paid RxDB Premium licence, and the hosted app.vendurepos.com you'd otherwise depend on has no named operator, maintainer or support/continuity statement anywhere on the site. That's the lock-in and abandonment risk I'd warn a client about.
overall_worst.where: home.desktop.02 footer / 'Before you start'; limitations.desktop.01 bullet 3; connect-a-till.desktop.01
overall_worst.fix: Add one line to the home page's 'Before you start': 'Use the hosted till at app.vendurepos.com, or self-build it, which needs a paid RxDB Premium licence.' Add one footer line naming who runs VendurePOS and the hosted app, with a link to the maintainer.
